raw_case_text: A 15-month-old female infant from Georgia arrived in France in September 2010. She had fever, sweats, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia and 213,000 Leishmania/ml. Leishmania amastigotes were observed in the bone marrow. There was no underlying immunosuppression. Treatment with 20 mg/kg of L-AmB resulted in complete resolution of symptoms and parasite clearance from the blood (PCR). Four months later, clinical symptoms recurred with 50 Leishmania/ml. The patient was treated with L-AmB then miltefosine for 28 days, resulting in complete clinical and parasitological response (Fig 1B). Five months later a second overt relapse occurred with typical symptoms and 20 Leishmania/ml. The patient was treated thereafter with meglumine antimoniate with a one-week break for QT interval prolongation. Upon EKG normalization, the course was reinstated with no further QT modifications. All VL clinical signs and laboratory abnormalities resolved. The patient remained relapse-free and PCR-negative 42 months of follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 15-month-old immunocompetent female infant from Georgia presented in September 2010 with fever, sweats, and hepatosplenomegaly, followed by two clinical and parasitological relapses of visceral leishmaniasis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The infant presented upon arrival in France from Georgia in September 2010 with fever, sweats, hepatosplenomegaly, and pancytopenia. She achieved initial clinical and PCR remission after liposomal amphotericin B (20 mg/kg), relapsed 4 months later (50 Leishmania/mL on blood qPCR) and responded to L-AmB followed by 28 days of oral miltefosine, and suffered a second overt clinical relapse 5 months thereafter (20 Leishmania/mL).
subjective.past_medical_history: 15-month-old female infant native to Georgia who arrived in France in September 2010; no underlying immunodeficiency.

objective.routine_investigations: Baseline pancytopenia; transient QT-interval prolongation on ECG during meglumine antimoniate therapy that normalized after a 1-week treatment interruption.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial bone marrow examination demonstrated Leishmania amastigotes, and quantitative blood PCR measured 213,000 Leishmania/mL at diagnosis, 50 Leishmania/mL at first relapse (month 4), and 20 Leishmania/mL at second relapse (month 9).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Bone marrow microscopy and serial quantitative blood PCR confirmed relapsing Visceral Leishmaniasis in an immunocompetent infant refractory to liposomal amphotericin B (20 mg/kg) and sequential L-AmB plus 28-day miltefosine. Salvage therapy with parenteral meglumine antimoniate (with a 1-week pause for reversible QT prolongation) achieved complete clinical, hematologic, and molecular cure, with the child remaining relapse-free and PCR-negative over 42 months of follow-up.
